title: Monetary Policy Report, July 13, 2018

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve submitted its semi-annual Monetary Policy Report to Congress on July 13, 2018, reaffirming its dual mandate (maximum employment and 2% inflation target measured by PCE) and its balanced approach when objectives conflict. The report covers economic developments through Q1 2018 and includes the Summary of Economic Projections showing a median longer-run normal unemployment rate estimate of 4.6%.
key_points: Reaffirms 2% inflation target measured by annual change in PCE price index as most consistent with statutory mandate
Describes inflation goal as symmetric — Committee would be concerned if inflation were running persistently above or below 2%
Maximum employment is largely determined by nonmonetary factors; no fixed goal is specified
Median of FOMC participants' estimates of longer-run normal unemployment rate was 4.6% (from most recent SEP projections at time of publication)
Policy decisions reflect longer-run goals, medium-term outlook, and assessments of balance of risks including financial stability risks
Information in report reflects data publicly available as of noon EDT July 12, 2018 (daily data through July 11; monthly through June 2018; quarterly through 2018:Q1)
why_it_matters: This semi-annual report to Congress defines the Federal Reserve's policy framework and strategic approach. It establishes the foundational context for ongoing monetary policy decisions — particularly the symmetric 2% PCE inflation target and the Committee's balanced approach to managing potential conflicts between employment and inflation objectives. The report signals how the Fed interprets its dual mandate and how it weights competing considerations.
macro_context: This report from July 2018 reflects the Fed's policy stance during a period of ongoing rate normalization following the financial crisis. At this time, the Fed was actively raising rates and the economy was in a late-expansion phase. The report discusses the Committee's framework for assessing the balance between maximum employment and price stability objectives. Historical context: this period preceded the 2018-2019 rate hikes that brought the target range to 2.25-2.50% before the pandemic-driven cuts.
important_numbers: 4.6% — median estimate of longer-run normal unemployment rate (from SEP projections)
2018:Q1 — end of quarterly data in report
